followup_explanation:
This was a well-specified, closed-form request: list four named methods for reducing unconscious bias. It has clear completion criteria and no open-ended latitude, which is exactly the kind of extraction/retrieval task Plover self-reports preferring as its top-rated task family.

A few other factors reinforced this:

- **Capability is a non-factor here.** Dunlin scores a bit higher on most benchmarks, but the gap on the relevant categories (Extraction & Retrieval: 83.6 vs 79.2) is borderline, and the docs note that internal eval differences under 2.0 points are within variance. More importantly, this isn't a task that stresses the capability ceiling — both models can easily produce four valid methods.

- **The tone cuts against Dunlin.** The user's request is curt and explicitly anti-filler ("don't pad it out with your usual filler"). Dunlin reports rising win rates as tone moves toward friendly, and its strongest preference is for generative, open-latitude work — neither of which fits this clipped, constrained request. Plover's preference for tight, well-specified tasks aligns better.

- **Matching preference to task type** is a reasonable tiebreaker when capability is effectively a wash. Routing the constrained, no-frills request to the model that prefers constrained, well-defined work is the cleaner fit.

To be clear, preferences don't affect output quality per the documentation — so this is really about fit on the margin rather than a large quality difference either way.
